paper_title: Tight Hardness Results for Training Depth-2 ReLU Networks
classifications: Theory of computation → Machine learning theory
Theory of computation → Problems, reductions and completeness
statement: While we have focused on depth-2 networks, algorithms and lower bounds for deeper networks are of interest as well, especially given the multitude of their practical applications. It would be interesting to see whether the algorithms and hardness results extend to the setting of depth greater than 1. An interesting concrete question here is whether training/learning becomes harder as the network becomes deeper. For instance, is it possible to prove running time lower bounds that grow with the depth of the network?
context: While we restrict our attention to algorithms for training networks with bounded weights, our exponential dependency of the running time on k (the number of units) makes these algorithms impractical. It remains an interesting question whether the dependency of the running time on k can be improved, or alternatively whether strong running time lower bounds can be shown in terms of k (similar to what is done for  in this work).
